functionalReqs: Place limit and market orders; cancel orders
Publish market data (order book depth, last trade)
Risk checks before an order enters the book
hints: Why do real exchanges run the matching engine single-threaded per symbol?
An order book per symbol: price levels with FIFO queues. Which data structures give O(1) best-price access and cancels?

Gateway → risk check → sequencer (assigns sequence numbers, writes to an event log) → matching engine per symbol shard (in memory) → execution reports and market data via multicast. Recovery by replaying the event log; hot standby replicas fed by the same sequence.
nonFunctionalReqs: Very low and predictable latency (p99 in microseconds to low ms)
No lost orders; full audit trail
problemStatement:
Design a **stock exchange**: brokers submit buy and sell orders, and a matching engine matches them by price-time priority and publishes trades and market data.

Latency is measured in microseconds, and the matching result must be deterministic and fair.
title: Design a Stock Exchange / Order Matching Engine
